title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $\alpha_1$ be the unique solution of the equation
		\begin{align}\label{3.3}
			E\left[L'\left(\alpha_1X\right)\right]=0
		\end{align} where $X\sim \text{Beta} \left(\frac{p_1+3}{2}, \frac{p_2-2}{2}\right)$. Then the risk of the estimator $\delta_{\phi_{01}(W)}$ is nowhere larger than that of the estimator $\delta_{\phi_1}$ provided $P\left(\phi_1(W)>d_0(W)\right)\neq 0$.

title: Corollary
body_md:
The risk of the estimator                                                                                                                                                                                        
		$\delta_{S1}=\min\left\{c_0,\frac{\alpha_1}{W} \right\}\frac{S_1}{S_2}$ dominates the BEE $\delta_{0}$ provided $P\left(\frac{\alpha_1}{c_0}<W\right)\neq 0$ holds true.
